To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new map framework is presented for SLAM in large-scale outdoor environments that is based on a graph of connected feature maps; and a new method is presented for robust data association in complex environments that is based solely on sensor data, without requiring a priori knowledge of robot location.
the following methods are effective for SLAM in extensive outdoor environments: (i) batch data association, (ii) correlation-based localisation, and (iii) network coupled feature maps. ii

a) a combined constraint data association method can be used for robust data association in large-scale SLAM even if the robot is lost; b) correlation-based localisation can be used for localisation when no discrete features are available; c) a network coupled feature maps framework can be used to solve the consistency and computational problems of large-scale SLAM; and d) the above three contributions can be used to perform SLAM over extensive outdoor environments.
